title: Tone and Style
description: Master controlling Claude's tone, formality, and voice to match your brand, audience, and purpose.

data.text: The same information communicated in different tones produces completely different effects. A customer support email written formally feels distant; the same email written warmly feels helpful. Claude can match almost any tone you specify — but only if you tell it explicitly. The default Claude tone is polite, slightly formal, and helpful. You need to direct it to match your specific needs.
How to Specify Tone in Prompts

Tone is best specified in two places: your custom instructions (for consistent tone across all conversations) and in individual prompts (for one-off adjustments). In the prompt, describe the tone using adjectives and examples. 'Write in a warm, conversational tone like a friendly expert explaining something to a colleague' is much more effective than 'write in a nice tone'.

data.title: Tone specification examples
data.content:
Corporate: 'Write in a professional, formal tone suitable for an executive summary. Avoid contractions and casual language.'

Friendly: 'Write in a warm, approachable tone like a helpful friend who knows the topic well. Use contractions and casual phrasing.'

Authoritative: 'Write in a confident, authoritative tone. State facts directly without hedging. Use the active voice.'

data.title: Tone presets you can copy into your custom instructions:
items: Professional — formal, precise, suitable for business communication
Conversational — warm, friendly, uses contractions and casual phrasing
Technical — precise, jargon-appropriate, structured for developers
Empathetic — warm, understanding, supportive, avoids jargon

data.text: When writing long documents with Claude, consistency matters. Claude can maintain a consistent tone throughout a long piece — but only if you remind it of the style periodically and use a custom instruction. For documents longer than a few thousand words, include a brief style reminder in the custom instruction and reference it in prompts.

data.title: Custom instruction for consistent tone
data.content: Custom instruction: 'When writing for my brand, use a professional but approachable tone. Avoid jargon unless the audience is technical. Use short paragraphs. End with a clear call to action. Maintain this style throughout all sections.'

data.title: Provide style samples
data.text: If you have existing writing that has the tone you want, paste a short sample into your custom instruction or include it in the prompt. Claude will mimic the style remarkably well.

You can change Claude's tone mid-conversation simply by stating the new tone in your next prompt. Claude adapts immediately because it processes each new message in the context of the conversation. This makes it easy to experiment with different tones for the same content.

data.title: Mid-conversation tone shift
data.content:
User: 'Write a product description for our new coffee maker.'
Claude: [Writes in default polite tone]
User: 'Now rewrite it in a playful, energetic tone like a social media influencer.'
Claude: [Rewrites with emojis, exclamation marks, and punchy language]

data.title: Tone and style takeaways
points: Be explicit about tone — describe it with adjectives and examples
Use custom instructions for consistent tone across conversations
Specify tone in individual prompts for one-off adjustments
Provide style samples for Claude to mimic
You can change tone mid-conversation by simply stating the new tone
